**Setup.** Let $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(1,1)$, $D=(0,1)$, and let $O=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ be the center. The condition requires that every point $P$ with all four angles strictly greater than $60^\circ$ lie in the open disk bounded by $\Gamma$. Call the set of such points $S$.

**Locus of $\angle APB>60^\circ$.** For a unit segment $AB$, the region where $\angle APB>60^\circ$ is the union of two disks of radius $r=1/\sqrt3$, centered at $(\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3})$. Points of the square's half-plane lie in the outer disk only if they lie in the inner one, so inside the square's half-plane the condition reduces to the inner disk. The four inner disks, all of radius $1/\sqrt3$, are centered at
$$E_{AB}=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}),\quad E_{BC}=(\tfrac12+\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3},\tfrac12),\quad E_{CD}=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12+\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}),\quad E_{DA}=(\tfrac12-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3},\tfrac12).$$
Points below $y=0$ or above $y=1$ (and similarly outside the other sides) cannot satisfy all four conditions, so
$$S = E_{AB}\cap E_{BC}\cap E_{CD}\cap E_{DA}.$$

**Vertices of $S$.** Adjacent inner disks meet at the corners of a smaller square. For example, $E_{BC}$ and $E_{CD}$ meet on the diagonal $y=x$ at $C$ and at $Q_A=(\tfrac12-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3},\tfrac12-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3})\approx(0.2113,0.2113)$. The four vertices $Q_A,Q_B,Q_C,Q_D$ are at distance
$$|Q_A-O|=\sqrt{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt6}$$
from $O$.

**Farthest point.** Each boundary arc of $S$ lies on a circle of radius $1/\sqrt3$ whose center is at distance $\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}$ from $O$. On such a circle the distance to $O$ is smallest at the point nearest $O$ and grows toward the far side, so along each arc the distance to $O$ is maximized at an endpoint. Hence $\sup_{P\in S}|P-O|=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$, attained only at the vertices $Q$.

**Check at a vertex.** At $Q_A$, $\angle APB=120^\circ$, $\angle BPC=60^\circ$, and the other two angles are also $\ge 60^\circ$ with the minimum equal to $60^\circ$. So $Q_A\notin S$, and $S$ lies strictly inside the closed disk of radius $1/\sqrt6$.

**Conclusion.** The circle of radius $1/\sqrt6$ centered at $O$ works, since $S$ lies in its open interior. No smaller circle works, since it would have to contain the four vertices $Q$ in its interior, which would require a larger radius. The minimum area is
$$\pi\cdot\frac16=\frac{\pi}{6},$$
so $a=1$, $b=6$, and $100a+b=106$.
